# ROB-001: Malformed JSON gets a -32700 Parse error

| Severity | Applies to | Spec section |
|---|---|---|
| warn | both eras, stdio, http | [2026-07-28/basic/index#messages](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/index#messages) |

Sends a request cut off in the middle of its JSON. All MCP messages MUST follow JSON-RPC 2.0, which answers unparsable input with error -32700 (Parse error) and id null. On Streamable HTTP a 4xx status is accepted too, with or without a JSON-RPC body. A warning, not an error: JSON-RPC 2.0 shows this answer in its examples rather than requiring it in a MUST, and many SDKs log the bad line and answer nothing. A server that crashes or stops answering after the input fails the run regardless, through the liveness probe that follows every case. Runs once per server.

From the command line: `mcpprobe checks explain ROB-001`. To leave it out of a run, add `"ROB-001"` to `[checks] disable` in [mcpprobe.toml](../configuration.md); to change how much it counts, use `severity_overrides`.
